description: Felixstowe Dock and Railway Company (FDRC), the harbour authority and operator of the Port of Felixstowe within Hutchison Ports UK, published this climate change adaptation report in August 2015 under the UK Adaptation Reporting Power, updating its first report of 2011. Coverage: the UK's busiest container port, handling over 4 million TEU a year and over 40% of UK container trade, with a channel dredged to 14.5 m, more than 2.3 km of continuous quay, 23 ship-to-shore cranes, roll-on roll-off ferries to Rotterdam and rail terminals with capacity above 1 million TEU a year on about six miles of port-owned track. Content: the statutory duties that climate could affect (facilities, conservancy, environment) and business risks from higher sea levels, stormier weather, wetter winters, hotter drier summers and heat waves, including flooding, coastal erosion, drainage and water shortage; it draws on Harwich Haven Authority's 2011 report for the shared approach channel and flags supply chain interdependencies for fuller study. Format and access: a 37-page PDF on GOV.UK. Licence and cost: free; no licence stated. Caveats: a qualitative self-assessment without hazard modelling. It gives asset and dependency context for climate adaptation and hazard exposure models of container ports and their rail links. It relates to the PLA and Heathrow adaptation reports in the catalogue.
